SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.35
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows (a) a very strong free O–H stretch at 3511 cm⁻¹, requiring at least one hydroxyl group; (b) three medium-intensity bands in the C–F stretching region 1000-1300 cm⁻¹ (1078, 1146, 1281 cm⁻¹), indicating the presence of one or more C–F bonds; (c) aromatic C–H stretch at 3082 cm⁻¹ and a ring C=C/C=N band at 1576 cm⁻¹, pointing to a hetero-aromatic ring; and (d) ring-breathing/ deformation bands at 732 and 864 cm⁻¹ typical of substituted six-membered N-heteroaromatics.  
Among the candidates, only molecules 1 and 5 contain both an –OH group and two C–F bonds. The additional ring nitrogen atoms in 1 (a difluoropyrimidinol) rationalize the relatively low-frequency intense band at 864 cm⁻¹ (pyrimidine ring breathing) and the 732 cm⁻¹ deformation more convincingly than the single-N pyridinol in 5. The remaining candidates lack either an OH group or C–F bonds, or show functional groups (multiple S–S, etc.) not supported by the spectrum. Therefore candidate 1 best matches the observed Raman features.
